title: PyTorch
line: Tensors, autograd and a training loop. Train and save a model.

project.title: A model that fits a noisy sine wave
project.brief: Train a PyTorch model on your own to fit a noisy sine curve. Make 1000 points, hold out 200 for validation, train from a DataLoader and save the trained model.
checks: The model subclasses nn.Module and trains from a DataLoader
Validation loss ends below a quarter of its first value
sine.pt is saved and loads into a fresh model

lessons.title: Tensors
lessons.goal: Teach PyTorch tensors in Jupyter. Make tensors with torch.tensor, torch.zeros and torch.rand, read shape and dtype, and move a 3 by 4 example to NumPy and back.
lessons.passes: A float32 tensor of shape (3, 4) prints and converts to a NumPy array and back.

lessons.title: Autograd
lessons.goal: Teach PyTorch autograd with requires_grad and backward by finding the gradient of a one-neuron squared error loss and comparing it with the gradient worked out by hand.
lessons.passes: w.grad matches the hand-worked gradient to within 1e-5.

lessons.title: Build a model with nn.Module
lessons.goal: Teach torch.nn.Module in PyTorch. Write a class with two nn.Linear layers, a tanh between them and a forward method for a 2-8-1 network, then count its parameters.
lessons.passes: The model has 33 parameters and returns shape (4, 1) for four samples.

lessons.title: Loss functions and optimizers
lessons.goal: Teach nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss and torch.optim.SGD in PyTorch by taking one training step on the four XOR points. Zero the gradients, call backward and step.
lessons.passes: The loss on the XOR points is lower after the optimizer step than before it.

lessons.title: Write the training loop
lessons.goal: Teach the PyTorch training loop. Train the 2-8-1 model on XOR with a forward pass, loss, zero_grad, backward and step in each epoch, and print the loss every 200 epochs.
lessons.passes: The printed loss falls and the model gets all four XOR points right.

lessons.title: Datasets and DataLoader
lessons.goal: Teach TensorDataset and DataLoader in PyTorch by wrapping 1000 random 2D points, labelled by whether they sit above a sine curve, and looping over shuffled batches of 32.
lessons.passes: The loader yields 32 batches and the first batch of points has shape (32, 2).

lessons.title: Hold out data and measure accuracy
lessons.goal: Teach evaluation in PyTorch with random_split, model.eval and torch.no_grad by holding out 200 of the points and printing validation accuracy after each epoch.
lessons.passes: Accuracy on the 200 held-out points is printed each epoch and ends above 0.9.

lessons.title: Use the Mac GPU
lessons.goal: Teach devices in PyTorch on a Mac. Pick mps when torch.backends.mps.is_available() is true and cpu otherwise, then move the model and every batch there with .to(device).
lessons.passes: The model's parameters and each batch are on the same chosen device.

lessons.title: Save and load a model
lessons.goal: Teach saving in PyTorch with torch.save, state_dict and load_state_dict by writing the trained model to model.pt and loading it into a fresh copy.
lessons.passes: model.pt exists and the reloaded model gives the same predictions.
